title: 10 Biggest Formula E Driver Transfers in Formula E History
excerpt:
From championship-winning transfers to shocking grid reshuffles, explore the moves that reshaped the sport.

With Mitch Evans making the bombshell move to Opel GSE Formula E Team this season, having started his Formula E career at Jaguar TCS Racing a decade ago, these are 10 of the biggest driver market swaps that have been seen in the championship since its inception.

From prominent promotions to the end of an era, there have been several signings that have shaped the success of the grid. As the 2026/27 Formula E grid starts to take shape, Championship Correspondent Katy Fairman picks her more significant driver swaps.

Wehrlein’s move to Porsche

The pairing of reigning World Champion Pascal Wehrlein and the Porsche Formula E team feels like a partnership that was always meant to be. Two giants of German motorsport, but when Wehrlein joined the all-electric championship for the 2018/19 season he was actually representing Mahindra Racing.

After competing in Formula 1 with the likes of Manor and Sauber, Wehrlein balanced a full-time Formula E seat with Development Driver duties for Scuderia Ferrari. He was teammates to Jérôme d'Ambrosio – who is now himself Deputy Team Principal for Ferrari in F1 – and secured one podium and a pole position during his rookie season.

He continued with Mahindra, but midway through the 2019/2020 season – which was disrupted by the coronavirus pandemic – he revealed on Instagram that he had left the Indian manufacturer with immediate effect.

Months later Porsche confirmed he would join the team as a full-time driver in their second season, and the rest is history. Two drivers’ World Championships and one Teams’ trophy later, the pairing of Wehrlein and Porsche is indisputably one of the strongest on the grid and will continue into GEN4.

Vergne departs DS

After eight seasons racing with the DS logo on his car, Jean-Eric Vergne made the switch to Citroën Racing for the 2025/26 season. The long-standing relationship started when JEV joined the DS Virgin Racing Team in 2015 for a single season, before leaving and joining the Techeetah team for the following season.

Following on from their championship-winning season with JEV, Techeetah brought on DS Automobiles from the 2018/19 season and the team won again – making Vergne the first two-time champion in Formula E history.

With four seasons racing under DS Techeetah, and another three as DS PENSKE, Vergne made the decision to leave the team in favour of Citroën Racing. Although both Citroën and DS run under the Stellantis banner, it still marked the end of a special partnership. JEV achieved a podium with the French team in their first season, and will continue with teammate Nick Cassidy in GEN4.

Buemi’s journey from e.Dams to Envision

Former Champion Sébastien Buemi joined Formula E for its inaugural season, which started with the 2014 Beijing E-Prix. Then racing for Renault e.dams, Buemi went on to establish himself as one of the best talents in the series and would win the 2015/16 championship after a tense final battle in Battersea, London.

Renault e.dams would continue, with Buemi at the helm, until 2018 when Nissan purchased a stake in the championship-winning racing organisation. It then became Nissan e.dams, but still Buemi stayed and picked up more silverware under the e.dams umbrella – 13 wins, 14 pole positions and 29 podiums in total.

However, after eight seasons and two generations of car, Buemi made the switch to Envision Racing for the 2022/23 season and remained there for the entire GEN3 era. It was a big change, but it didn’t stop the Swiss racing legend from building on his excellent racing record with another victory over the 2025 Monaco E-Prix, as well as plenty of pole positions and podiums.

Evans exits Jaguar for Opel

Perhaps the biggest driver move we have seen in Formula E’s history, Mitch Evans announced his departure from Jaguar TCS Racing after ten years together earlier this year. The Kiwi is the World Championship’s most successful driver in terms of victories, and was loyal to the Jaguar squad since he – and the team – joined the series in 2016/17.

Interview: Mitch Evans on his new journey with Opel GSE in Formula E

Having achieved all his silverware and milestones with Jaguar, Evans confirmed the switch to the Stellantis-powered Opel team for GEN4. As a new manufacturer on the grid, and a new powertrain to learn, this will be a big change for Evans but he says it comes at the right time and he’s ready for the challenge.

“GEN4 was a big reason why I wanted to move,” Evans explained last month. “I decided that I will look elsewhere, and there was some good interest from a lot of top teams. I have considered it in the past, and it's not the first time I've considered leaving Jaguar, although it's the first time I've really acted on it. I was with one team for so long, and you are always intrigued to see what other offers are out there or what other teams are up to.”

Di Grassi’s Audi adventure ends

The now-retired Lucas di Grassi had a relationship with Audi in endurance racing for several years, before he signed up to their Formula E programme for the first race. Having competed in the World Endurance Championship for the German marque, di Grassi signed on to race for the Audi Sport ABT Formula E Team and win championships with them – both a drivers’ title for him and the 2017/18 teams’ honours.

Whilst racing with the Audi badge in Formula E, di Grassi managed 12 wins, three pole positions and 35 podiums.

However, after 84 races Audi departed the all-electric championship and di Grassi moved over to the Monaco-based Venturi team. Here he would take a victory in the 2021/22 season, and four podiums, before stints with Mahindra, ABT and Lola before announcing his retirement ahead of the GEN4 era.

Müller's Porsche promotion

Nico Müller also joined the Porsche Formula E Team last season, and was recently announced as continuing with the reigning Manufacturers' Champion into GEN4 alongside teammate Pascal Wehrlein.

After five seasons in Formula E, and one rogue podium at the 2021 Valencia E-Prix, Müller’s results didn’t reflect the high-quality driver he is.

However, this all changed for his sixth – and most recent – season, when the Swiss driver completed his first season for the Porsche team where he achieved his maiden Formula E win in Berlin, as well as his first pole position in Miami.

De Vries' return with Mahindra

Having stuck with Mercedes-EQ for his first three years in Formula E, and winning the 2020/21 Drivers’ World Championship title in the process – both Nyck de Vries and the manufacturer left the championship in 2022.

During this time, de Vries found himself in Formula 1 racing and competed in 11 Grands Prix from 2022 to 2023, racing for both Williams Racing and AlphaTauri. But, after a change of circumstance, the Dutch driver found himself back in the Formula E paddock for the London E-Prix finale in 2023.

Months later it was confirmed that the former World Champion would return to electric racing, and partner up with Edoardo Mortara at the Mahindra Racing team. Three seasons later, and the duo have just had a contract extension announced, with de Vries helping the team achieve their first win of the GEN3 in Monaco before adding to the trophy cabinet with another win in Tokyo. The news of his return made international headlines, and it’s a partnership that is still going strong on both sides of the Mahindra garage.

Bird joins Jaguar

Another big storyline was the signing of Sam Bird to the Jaguar organisation, ahead of the 2020/21 season – the first campaign as an official FIA World Championship. Bird had been a part of Formula E since its inaugural season, racing for the ‘Virgin Racing’ team for six solid seasons. During that time, he had won a race in every campaign he’d competed in and was the only driver to have done so.

At the time of Bird’s announcement, Jaguar had totalled up two victories in Formula E – both thanks to Evans – but had never really had a strong ‘second’ driver. That was until Bird.

His signing made Jaguar one of the most competitive line-ups on the grid, and their choice was instantly rewarded when Bird brought home their two and only victories that season, and alongside Evans helped deliver second-place honours in the teams’ championship with their best result having been sixth in the standings years prior.

Cassidy connects with Citroën

Although Nick Cassidy’s start in Formula E came with two years at Envision with Audi powertrains, he moved to racing with the Jaguar package from the GEN3 era and progressed up to the works team by the 2023/24 season.

Tensions were high in Cassidy’s final season with Jaguar TCS Racing, so news of his departure didn’t seem too much of a surprise. Nevertheless, it brought a lot of speculation as to where he would go. As the man who won the most races in the GEN3 era, Cassidy’s stocks were high and his move to the new Citroën team was quite the risk.

Yes, Citroën has been hugely successful in almost all its motorsport conquests, but for their first voyage into single-seaters, there was a lot to learn. That analogy was quickly out the window, when Cassidy delivered the team their first podium in São Paulo last season, before achieving their maiden win in front of the passionate fans in Mexico City.

Ticktum's turn at Fortescue Zero

Dan Ticktum will be joining Fortescue Zero Racing for GEN4, a change that might not look too dramatic on the outside but actually has layers.

Ever since Ticktum joined in 2021/22 with NIO 333, he’s remained part of the same ‘team’ despite it going through multiple rebrands and powertrain suppliers: NIO became ERT, which then became CUPRA KIRO. His departure to the new Fortescue Zero squad marked the end of that era for the Silverstone-based team.

How will he manage at the all-new Australian team, as a customer of Jaguar powertrains? Make sure you're watching the first GEN4 season to find out.

Other notable driver moves

In addition to the above, there have also been some significant signings that have changed a driver’s career path, or are yet to play out.

Nelson Piquet Jr’s – the inaugural FIA Formula E champion – moved to Jaguar for the 2017/18 season, after leaving the China Racing/NEXTEV team that he won the championship with in that first season. Unfortunately, he left midway through the 2018–19 season, and was replaced by Alex Lynn.

Andre Lotterer left a successful team at DS Techeetah alongside Vergne, and after helping win the Teams’ Championship in 2018–19, in exchange for a seat at the new Porsche Formula E team alongside Neel Jani. Lotterer would complete three seasons for the team before being replaced by Antonio Felix da Costa.

Speaking of da Costa, his move to Jaguar TCS Racing last season felt like the start of something new. The 2019/2020 Champion has raced with many teams in the all-electric championship, from BMW Andretti, Porsche and DS Techeetah, but seemed ready for a new chapter with the British team and has been rewarded with two victories and a further three podiums last season.

title: “This Car is a Game Changer”: Pourchaire Gears up For Formula E Step With Opel
excerpt:
Théo Pourchaire is preparing to embark on a new chapter in his racing career, joining Opel GSE Formula E Team for its entry into the all-electric championship.

The Rüsselsheim-based manufacturer made headlines when it announced its arrival in Formula E at a press conference ahead of the 2026 Madrid E-Prix. With decades of motorsport experience spanning rallying, touring cars and endurance racing, Opel is now setting its sights on the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship, marking a significant new chapter in the brand’s racing history.

FIRST LOOK: Opel steps into Formula E's GEN4 era with the GSE 27FE

For Pourchaire, the opportunity to represent one of Germany’s most recognisable automotive manufacturers marks an exciting step in his career. Speaking at the unveiling of the Opel GSE 27FE at the Paris Motor Show, the Frenchman shared his thoughts of the team’s new look.

He said, “My first thoughts when I saw the livery, is that it’s a very classy livery that represents Opel at its very best, I love it.

"My favourite part, I would say is the yellow, because yellow is a colour that has been on my helmet since the beginning of my racing career, so I'm matching well with Opel.

"Opel is a very important German manufacturer, and it's a legendary car brand, it's been here for a very, very long time. I'm really proud to be representing Opel, and I'm really happy to see them, in my country, at the Paris Motor Show."

Although the 23-year-old will be a newcomer to the Formula E grid, he is no stranger to the demands of top-level motorsport. The Frenchman has built an impressive résumé across single-seater and endurance racing, establishing himself as one of the most accomplished young drivers of his generation.

His rise through the junior ranks began with victory in French Formula 4 in 2018, followed by the ADAC Formula 4 title in 2019. He subsequently made his mark in the FIA Formula 2, where he claimed the 2023 title with one race victory and 10 podium finishes across his championship winning campaign.

Beyond single-seaters, Pourchaire has made a name for himself in the world of endurance racing, with appearances in the 24 Hours of Le Mans, the European Le Mans Series (ELMS) and the FIA World Endurance Championship (WEC).

His Formula One experience has also been an important part of his development. Pourchaire previously served as a reserve driver for Sauber/Stake Formula One Team, taking part in a F1 test in August 2021. He later continued in a test driver role with Alfa Romeo before joining Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team as a development driver.

Now, with a full-time seat on the horizon in the all-electric championship, Pourchaire faces a fresh challenge: adapting his experience to Formula E's next-generation electric machinery while helping newcomer Opel establish itself in the championship.

He said: ‘Working with the Opel family has been a real pleasure so far. I've met a lot of people, the mechanics and engineers, but also the marketing and communications team. It's a lot of new faces, but I'm really enjoying it.

“There's a lot of work behind the scenes: a lot of simulator sessions, a lot of meetings with the engineers and with the mechanics to get to know my cockpit. After all, it's a completely different car for me. It's a new car (for Formula E), and it's going to be like a completely new championship for everyone.

“Of course, it is still the Formula E World Championship, but this car is a game changer. It’s a lot of work behind the scenes with engineers, even with the mechanics, just to get to know my cockpit as well.”

Formula E has been on Pourchaire’s radar for several years. His first taste of the championship’s machinery came in 2022, when he undertook three days of testing in a GEN3 car on behalf of Spark. Since then, he has continued to build on his knowledge of the all-electric championship, including rookie free practice sessions in Jeddah and Berlin with Maserati MSG Racing and more recently, in January 2026, Citroën Racing selected him for free practice sessions in Miami and Madrid.

His performance in Miami earlier this year was particularly noteworthy, the Frenchman finishing the session in second, just 0.093s off the fastest time - immediately demonstrating his potential against a field of established Formula E talent.

That experience has helped prepare him for the next major step: the arrival of GEN4, which promises a significant leap in performance and represents one of Formula E’s most exciting innovations so far. The new machinery is capable of delivering 50% more power in race mode than the GEN3 Evo, with peak output reaching up to 600 kW (816 hp) in qualifying and ATTACK MODE. For drivers making the transition, the increase in performance presents both an exciting opportunity and a steep learning curve.

READ MORE: GEN4 Unleashed - everything you need to know about Formula E's new era

He asserted, “My first impression about this car is that it's so powerful. The power is crazy. I think it's the race car that accelerates the most that I've tried in my career. It’s also much quicker than the GEN3 in the corners, and it's better looking. It 's going to be a real pleasure to be part of this championship.

"The testing with the new GEN4 car has been going well at the moment. It's a new car for everybody, so a lot of learning, a lot of ups and downs, but we are working really hard with everybody to make sure that we are competitive."

title: Who’s On the Grid? Formula E’s 2026/27 Driver Lineup So Far
excerpt:
Ahead of the 2026/27 season – and the start of Formula E's GEN4 era – here are the drivers confirmed to be racing on the grid.

Ahead of Pre-Season Testing in Jarama, Madrid, next month, these are the drivers that have secured race seats for the 2026/27 Formula E season – the first of the all-new and exciting GEN4 era.

From respected rookies, big driver changes and the return of lots of familiar faces, these are all the drivers that will be taking to the track for the first-taste of GEN4 across the 2026/27 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship season when the season starts on 18 December in Jeddah.

Who are the new drivers this season?

Currently, there are two new names with full-time Formula E seats for next season. First to be announced is French driver Théo Pourchaire with the Opel GSE Formula E Team. Known as one of racing’s brightest talents, Pourchaire works as a Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team Development Driver and is a former Formula 2 World Champion.

Elsewhere, Paysafe Envision Racing announced Zak O'Sullivan would be promoted to a full-time seat, after the Brit has been the team’s Simulator Driver and participated in several Rookie Tests for them over the GEN3 era. O'Sullivan has also been busy in Super Formula this year, and won the prestigious Autosport BRDC Award in 2021.

What are the big driver changes in Formula E this season?

A new era of the all-electric championship resulted in quite the driver market reshuffle, with lots of drivers changing teams during our off-season. Dan Ticktum has relocated to the new Fortescue Zero Racing team, Zane Maloney has moved to Nissan and Mitch Evans departed Jaguar TCS Racing after a decade to switch things up with the new Opel entry. Maximilian Gunther has also joined Envision for the new season, with Jake Hughes returning after a year out and partnering up with CUPRA KIRO.

There are a few slots still to be decided before pre-season testing starts on 16 November 2026, so be sure to keep coming back to the website or follow our socials for all the latest.

Andretti Formula E

Drivers: Jake Dennis and Felipe Drugovich

Andretti have retained the same driver line-up as last season, bringing back 2022/23 World Champion Jake Dennis who signed a multi-year deal with the team earlier this year. Dennis, who won his title with the Andretti squad, managed two wins, two pole positions and six podiums with the American outfit last season.

On the other side of the garage, Brazilian Felipe Drugovich will return for a second season in Formula E. In his debut season, the Formula 2 champion managed a podium and pole position, and will look to add to that tally in the GEN4 era.

Citroën Racing

Drivers: Nick Cassidy and Jean-Eric Vergne

Another unchanged line-up for the 2026/27 season is Citroën Racing, who have continued with their driver pairing. Two-time Formula E Champion Jean-Eric Vergne is now the grid’s most experienced driver, having started 163 races during his time here with 11 wins and 39 podiums to his name ahead of the start of GEN4.

For Nick Cassidy, last season was a successful one with five podiums and a win for Citroën in their first season of single seater racing. Cassidy stood on the top step of the podium 11 times during the GEN3 era, making him the most successful driver of that era of Formula E.

CUPRA KIRO

Drivers: Pepe Martí and Jake Hughes

Josep Maria "Pepe" Martí will be back for another season at CUPRA KIRO, after a brilliant rookie year at the team last season. The Spanish superstar – and former Red Bull Junior – banked two podiums and 66 points in his first Formula E campaign, and impressed a lot of the paddock.

He will be teammates with Jake Hughes, who returns to the Formula E World Championship after a year out. The Briton is rapid, which can be seen from his four pole positions in Formula E before GEN4 and has been able to collect two podiums during his 47 race starts to date, racing for McLaren and Maserati. After being a Reserve and Simulator driver for Mahindra Racing last season, Hughes is back in a full-time seat at CUPRA KIRO.

Fortescue Zero Racing

Drivers: Taylor Barnard and Dan Ticktum

Formula E’s first Australian team has picked two of the most talented drivers on the grid for their debut season. First up is Taylor Barnard, who has more records to his name than most drivers combined. From youngest-ever Formula E race winner – which he achieved in London earlier this year – to youngest race starter, youngest points scorer, youngest podium finisher and youngest pole position holder, Barnard has ticked them all off and hopes to add to his trophy cabinet for Fortescue Zero in GEN4.

His teammate will be Dan Ticktum, who makes the swap from CUPRA KIRO to Fortescue Zero this season. The two-time race winner has been a part of Formula E for several seasons now, and is known for his pure speed with three pole positions and the person chosen to drive the GEN4 up the iconic Goodwood Hill across this year’s Festival of Speed.

Jaguar TCS Racing

Drivers: Antonio Felix da Costa and TBC

So far at Jaguar TCS Racing, only one driver has been locked in. 2019/20 Champion Antonio Felix da Costa returns for a second year with the squad, and will have a new teammate after the departure of Mitch Evans after 10 years at the team. The Portuguese racer is one of the championship’s most experienced pairs of hands, and in his first season with Jaguar managed five podiums and two wins – with the latter being added to give him 14 Formula E wins, the joint-second highest of any driver in the history of the championship.

Lola Formula E Team

Drivers: TBC and TBC

As it stands, the Lola Formula E Team have yet to announce who they will be signing for the first season of GEN4. After the retirement of Lucas di Grassi from racing and the departure of Zane Maloney, the iconic racing team are guaranteed to bring in two different drivers for their 2026/27 campaign.

Mahindra Racing

Drivers: Nyck de Vries and Edoardo Mortara

There will be no change at the Mahindra Racing team, as they opt to keep their excellent driver pairing for another season. 2020/21 World Champion Nyck de Vries will be back for another year of racing in Formula E, and hoping to add to his solid 2025/26 campaign, where he picked up two wins for Mahindra – ending a four-year drought for the team – and four podiums.

Also at Mahindra is Edoardo Mortara, who has 128 career race starts to his name after making his Formula E debut almost a decade ago. During that time he’s managed six wins, seven pole positions – four of which were last season – and 18 podiums.

Nissan Formula E Team

Drivers: Oliver Rowland and Zane Maloney

There is some change at Nissan for the 2026/27 season, with the new addition of Zane Maloney. The boy from Barbados has been on the Formula E grid for the last two seasons, and moves up to the Japanese manufacturer – and one of the championship’s most successful teams – for the GEN4 era. After stints in Formula 3 and Formula 2 before joining the Formula E grid full-time, Maloney is tipped as one to watch in GEN4.

On the other side of the garage, the partnership between 2024/25 World Champion Oliver Rowland and Nissan continues. For Rowland, who made his debut at the 2015 Punta del Este E-Prix, it has been a rollercoaster journey in the all-electric championship. 112 race starts, 10 podiums, eight wins and one World Championship later, Rowland is back with Nissan to collect more silverware in this new era, in a role he balances alongside being a manager and mentor to Racing Bull's driver Arvid Lindblad in Formula 1.

Opel GSE Formula E Team

Drivers: Mitch Evans and Théo Pourchaire

One of the biggest moves in Formula E history sees Mitch Evans start a new chapter at the Opel GSE Formula E Team this season. Opel, who are new to the championship this season, have signed Evans after he completed a decade at the Jaguar team. For Evans – who has banked the most wins of any driver during his time in Formula E – he says this new start has come at the right time in his racing career.

As well as experience, Opel have opted for youth with big junior talent Théo Pourchaire joining the Formula E grid in 2026/27. In addition to his former responsibilities as Citroën’s Rookie and Test driver last season, Pourchaire has also been racing in the World Endurance Championship – like a lot of our grid – and was the 2023 FIA Formula 2 Champion.

Paysafe Envision Formula E Team

Drivers: Maximilian Guenther and Zak O'Sullivan

The Paysafe Envision Formula E Team have opted for a fresh new line-up for the first season of GEN4, bringing in Maximilian Guenther on one side of their very green team garage. The German, who has seven wins across his time in the championship, has raced for several teams up and down the grid and is one of the most adaptable talents out there.

The team have also promoted Zak O'Sullivan after several years of using him as their Simulator and Rookie driver. Having raced in Japan this year – competing in both Super Formula and Super GT – GT300 – O'Sullivan is no stranger to single-seaters, having raced in FIA Formula 2 and 3, as well as completing a Formula 1 Free Practice session with Williams Racing in 2023.

Porsche Formula E Team

Drivers: Pascal Wehrlein and Nico Müller

For the factory Porsche Formula E Team – and the reigning Manufacturers’ Champions – the driver line-up remains unchanged. Current World Champion Pascal Wehrlein will be back with the Porsche team, having become the second person to secure more than one drivers’ title in Formula E. With three wins last season, six podiums and four pole positions, the pairing of two German giants clearly works and the trophy cabinet is proof of that.

Nico Müller has also been a brilliant addition to the Porsche team, and last season earned his first victory in the all-electric championship in one of their machines. It’s a strong driver pairing, and will continue into the first season of the GEN4 era.

Porsche's second team entry for the 2026/27 season has not yet confirmed any driver signings.

title: Dan Ticktum to race with Fortescue Zero Racing for 2026/27 season
excerpt:
The 27-year-old will partner Taylor Barnard at Fortescue Zero Racing for the 2026/27 season - the first campaign of the GEN4 era.

A Formula E fan favourite, Dan Ticktum has competed in the all-electric championship since the 2021/22 season, sticking with CUPRA KIRO through their evolution from NIO 333 and ERT Formula E Team into their current identity.

Along the way, Ticktum has gained praise across the paddock for his strong one-lap pace, daring race winning manoeuvres, and honest assessment of his own performances. This evident talent has seen the Brit collect two E-Prix victories to date.

The first of these came at the 2025 Jakarta E-Prix, where a late-race crash between Jake Dennis and Nyck de Vries allowed Ticktum to sneak into the lead and hold firm to the chequered flag. A second victory followed at the 2026 Tokyo E-Prix, thanks to an epic last-lap overtake around Turn 16 on Dennis - who suffered a momentary power cut.

Now, as Formula E prepares to enter the all-new GEN4 era, Ticktum embarks on a new challenge, joining forces with Fortescue Zero Racing for the upcoming 2026/27 season. The Australian squad boasts an all-British line-up, with Ticktum joined by Formula E's most-recent race winner, Taylor Barnard.

With two race winning drivers in the squad, the team will be looking to put together an impressive debut campaign when the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship returns for a record-breaking 21-race calendar.

title: Porsche to continue with Wehrlein and Müller for GEN4
excerpt:
With the GEN4 era fast approaching, the reigning Manufacturers' Champions have opted for consistency in their driver line-up.

As one of the most successful teams in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship, Porsche know what it takes to win. Following a dominant stretch that brought driver and manufacturer world titles back to Germany, Porsche is locking in continuity behind the wheel for the championship's most exciting era to date.

Capable of reaching speeds in excess of 335kph, 0-100kph in approximately 1.8 seconds, and 0-200kph in just 4.4 seconds - 1.5 seconds faster than its predecessor - GEN4 will deliver 50% more power in race mode than the current GEN3 Evo race car. The GEN4 car will be an average of 10 seconds faster per lap than the GEN3 car in qualifying mode. In ATTACK MODE, GEN4 produces up to 600kW of power, a 71% increase in base output over GEN3 Evo, delivering performance that pushes the limits of electric racing. GEN4 is the only single-seater race car with permanent all-wheel drive.

READ MORE: Everything you need to know about Formula E's GEN4 era

Despite some ups and downs along the way, Wehrlein's 2025/26 Formula E season culminated in a masterclass of consistency and speed as he claimed his second Drivers' World Championship with the Porsche outfit. On the path to his coronation, Wehrlein recorded three E-Prix victories and secured six podium finishes - results which established his position as a championship protagonist throughout the season.

Meanwhile, Müller's 2025/26 campaign with Porsche marked a career-defining breakthrough, as the Swiss driver proved to be a critical asset alongside teammate Wehrlein. Over the course of the season, he delivered some impressive performances, including a second-place at the Miami E-Prix and a dominant victory at the Berlin E-Prix in front of Porsche's jubilant home crowd.

With a proven champion in Wehrlein and proven race winner in Müller behind-the-wheel, the German squad has locked in an impressive line-up to defend their crowns and dominate the fastest, most exciting chapter in the world's leading all-electric championship.

title: From heartbreak to history: Pascal Wehrlein’s journey to two-time Formula E Champion
excerpt:
11 Wins, 24 Podiums, 2 Titles: the defining Formula E career highlights of Pascal Wehrlein

In one of the most unpredictable finishes in Formula E history, Pascal Wehrlein clinched his second Drivers' World Championship, as a nine-driver title battle came down to the final moments of the season in London.

Across his eight-year career in the all-electric series - and three generations of Formula E machinery - the German-Mauritian driver has achieved 11 victories, 24 podiums, and 883 laps led.

We take a look back at some of his Formula E highlights and uncover what truly makes him a champion.

The move to Mahindra

His success as the youngest driver to win the DTM championship opened the door to Formula 1, where he debuted with Manor Racing in 2016, before moving to Sauber the following year, for what would be his final season in the championship. However, after briefly returning to DTM in 2018, he transitioned to Formula E with Mahindra Racing, joining the team on the first day of 2018/19 pre-season testing in Valencia.

When the season got underway, Wehrlein immediately impressed, scoring his first-ever Formula E podium in just the third round of the season at the 2019 Santiago E-Prix. In the following round, he also came painfully close to clinching his maiden victory in a chaotic Mexico City E-Prix.

The German driver secured his maiden pole and led the field for the majority of the race, with Oliver Rowland and Lucas di Grassi breathing down his neck and applying pressure. He fought hard, but di Grassi wouldn’t give him a moment’s respite. Heading into the final lap in front of almost 40,000 fans, Wehrlein ran out of energy heading out of the final turn, allowing the Brazilian to slip through and cross the line first.

He finished his rookie season on 58 points, just nine points behind his then more senior teammate, Jerome d’Ambrosio. The partnership would continue to the following season, where he finished 18th on the standings, with fourth place as his best result.

Triumph in Mexico

Wehrlein would soon find a home with TAG Heuer Porsche for the 2020/21 Formula E season. His first campaign with the German automotive giant was a story of missed opportunities, with technical infringements costing both him and the team a potential maiden victory at the 2021 Puebla E-Prix, despite Wehrlein crossing the line first after starting from pole position. The following day brought further frustration: Wehrlein finished second but was demoted to fourth after a five-second penalty for improper use of FANBOOST.

Heading into the following season, Wehrlein had plenty to prove. Having being denied victory in Mexico City twice, the 2022 E-Prix finally offered a different ending. Starting from pole position, he initially led the race before dropping behind Edoardo Mortara and Jean-Eric Vergne as the leading group battled for position. Rather than forcing his way through prematurely, Wehrlein focused on energy efficiency, keeping enough in reserve to attack when it mattered most.

With 15 minutes on the clock, Wehrlein and then teammate Andre Lotterer, made their move, passing Vergne and then Mortara, to reclaim the lead of the race with a comfortable nine second gap to their rivals. Wehrlein then controlled the closing stages, with Lotterer following him across the line to complete a historic one-two finish. It was Wehrlein’s first Formula E win and Porsche’s first in the all-electric championship since entering the series in 2019.

Two victories within 24 hours

The beginning of the GEN3 era saw Wehrlein firmly established as a title contender. After finishing second behind Andretti’s Jake Dennis in the Mexico City season opener, he arrived in Diriyah ready to fight back.

The Saudi Arabian double-header would become one of the defining weekends of his Formula E career.

Qualifying for the first race proved challenging, leaving the Porsche driver ninth on the grid. But while others fought for position through the opening corners, he made up ground quickly, navigating the early chaos and working his way into the top six. He then timed his ATTACK MODE activations effectively, using the additional power to move through the field while preserving enough energy for the closing stages.

The decisive move came on Lap 30 at Turn 16, when Wehrlein passed Jaguar’s Sam Bird for the lead. From there, he had to withstand pressure from championship leader Jake Dennis, who had also fought his way through the pack. Wehrlein managed his energy and pace superbly to hold off the Andretti driver and secure his first win of the season.

Just 24 hours later, Wehrlein returned to the grid in fifth, with Dennis starting sixth. Once again, the German driver demonstrated that qualifying position would not dictate his afternoon. He made up places early, remained patient as the leaders cycled through their ATTACK MODE activations, and waited for the right moment to strike.

As the leading group reshuffled, Wehrlein seized the advantage and moved into the lead, with Dennis once again emerging as his closest challenger. The Porsche driver held firm through the closing laps to claim his second consecutive victory, which promoted him to the top of the Driver’s Championship - granting Porsche an early advantage in the title fight.

Despite this impressive start to the season, Wehrlein ultimately finished fourth in Drivers' standings with 149 points, adding two further victories to his tally and consistently finishing inside the top-10.

2023/24 Season finale: Wehrlein vs Evans

The 2023/24 season was Wehrlein’s strongest campaign yet. He opened the season with victories in Mexico and Misano and maintained his consistency throughout the year. However, despite his strong form, the title fight went down to the wire, with the London E-Prix double-header set to decide the championship.

Wehrlein started third on the grid, while Mitch Evans stormed away from pole position. It took Wehrlein 16 laps to find the perfect opportunity to slip past Envision Racing’s Sebastian Buemi and take the lead from the Jaguar TCS Racing driver, making the most out of his ATTACK MODE. He held on to secure his third victory of the season, but the title fight was far from over, with Wehrlein holding just a three-point advantage over Evans on 177 points. ,

The final round delivered the expected drama. Nick Cassidy kicked off from pole, with Evans starting third and Wehrlein fourth. The equation was simple: whichever contender finished ahead of the other would have a crucial advantage in the title fight.

By Lap 11, Evans was still looking strong, but Wehrlein was breathing down his neck, with both drivers running near the front of the pack. The turning point came when contact involving Cassidy and Antonio Felix da Costa damaged the Jaguar driver’s hopes of securing the title, leaving Evans and Wehrlein to fight for the crown.

Wehrlein ultimately crossed the line second behind Oliver Rowland, with Evans finishing third. Despite not winning the race, the result was enough to secure the Drivers’ World Championship for Wehrlein, who finished the season on 198 points, just six ahead of Evans.

Champions are made under pressure

Fast forward to the 2025/26 Formula E season finale in London, and Wehrlein arrived at the British capital just five points behind championship leader Jake Dennis and three points behind second-placed Mitch Evans, leaving everything to play for in the final two rounds.

The 31-year-old driver delivered when it mattered most, taking victory from pole position in the penultimate race after making all the right decisions. He crossed the line five seconds ahead of Dennis, setting up a final showdown between the pair in the final race of the GEN3 era.

READ MORE: Best final lap drama from the 2025/26 Formula E season

The final qualifying session of the year proved successful for Wehrlein, as he lined up third on the grid, while Evans started fifth and Dennis could only manage 16th. It was a difficult position for the Andretti driver, but Evans was still eyeing his long-awaited championship crown. For Evans, the equation was simple: he needed to win, and hope that Wehrlein finished outside the points. And as the race unfolded, things began to fall into place for the Jaguar driver - could he do the impossible?

In the race, Wehrlein dropped out of the top five and gradually slipped to 11th, while Evans moved ahead of his teammate, da Costa, to climb to fourth. The Jaguar drivers also had another target in sight, with the team fighting to secure its second Teams’ Championship. With just two laps remaining, contact involving Dennis and Wehrlein disrupted both drivers’ races. Although both managed to return to the track, there was little time left to make up the lost ground.

Evans ultimately finished fourth, but it was not enough to overturn Wehrlein’s advantage in the standings. The German had done enough to claim his second Drivers’ World Championship, while Porsche also secured the Manufacturers’ Title.

Heading into GEN4 as our reigning champion, what's next for Pascal Wehrlein?

title: "Finishing on a high": Sébastien Buemi reflects on his final Formula E weekend
excerpt:
Sebastien Buemi called time on his illustrious Formula E career (for now) after the 2026 London E-Prix, with his future in the all-electric championship now set to take a different direction.

The 37-year-old Swiss driver has been a mainstay of the Formula E paddock since its inaugural season in 2014, and is one of only four drivers to have raced in every season, alongside Antonio Felix da Costa, Jean-Eric Vergne, and Lucas di Grassi.

He finishes his Formula E career with 160 starts, 14 victories, 36 podiums, and one Drivers’ Championship title, which he won in the 2015/16 season. He also remains in the Formula E history book as the most successful driver at the Monaco E-Prix, with three wins in 2015, 2017, and 2025 - one more than the only two-time victor, Oliver Rowland.

A permanent place within the Paysafe Envision family

Buemi joined Paysafe Envision Formula E (previously Envision Racing) at the start of the 2022/23 season, finishing sixth in the Drivers’ Championship that year, whilst his third-place finish in the London E-Prix season finale helped the British team secure its first and, as of the end of the 2025/26 campaign, only Teams’ Championship.

READ MORE: Paysafe Envision reveal new livery for 2026/27 Formula E season

The following year, Buemi finished 15th in the standings, but again ended the year on a high with a podium in London, his second trip to the rostrum in the 2023/24 season. 2024/25's campaign gave Buemi his long-awaited 14th Formula E victory, after winning the Monaco E-Prix for the third time - solidifying his status as the all-electric 'Mr Monaco'.

This season, however, was one of highs and lows for Buemi, who entered the London finale with 75 championship points and only one podium finish from the season, despite a relatively consistent run of finishes inside the top- ten.

At the London E-Prix double-header, the final race weekend of the 2025/26 season and the last races of the GEN3 era, he impressed in Saturday's race, starting from P10 and using the Full Course Yellow period to his advantage as both Lola Yamaha ABT’s drivers, Zane Maloney and Lucas di Grassi, ended up in the wall. Though he narrowly missed out on a podium, he managed to take home fourth whilst his teammate Joel Eriksson finished 14th.

Reflecting on the race, he said, “I always do the best I can, and then move on, no more special feeling.” He continued, “I’m happy to score a few points. Obviously, Saturday was a crazy race, like it is always here in London.

“I'm lucky with the strategy, we pitted under the Full Course Yellow, but at the same time, I had the ATTACK MODE, so I did lose a bit of hope. It feels like P3 would have been possible with the perfect race, but at the end of the day, I'm quite happy with that result.

“I always have a different mindset. We take it step by step, session by session. In this category, so many things can happen. I'm not too bothered. I just do the best I can and then at the end of the day we count whether we score points or not.”

Sunday’s race was chaotic, to say the least, with much of the attention focused on the three championship protagonists. Porsche’s Pascal Wehrlein ultimately came out on top of Andretti’s Jake Dennis and Jaguar TCS Racing’s Mitch Evans, securing his second World Championship title.

READ MORE: Pascal Wehrlein wins his second Formula E Drivers' World Championship

Amidst the chaos, Buemi kept his cool. On Lap 13, he activated his four-minute ATTACK MODE, which helped him climb to P6. His teammate Eriksson made contact with the reigning champion on the same lap, forcing him out of the race. Buemi, meanwhile, continued to fight at the front and held on to claim fifth in his final appearance behind-the-wheel of the GEN3 car with the Envision squad.

“I don't think I could have done much better, so I'm happy with that result," he said. "Finishing on a high, quite a few points, 22 points this weekend. So I feel like I've done my job.”

“It's much better than having a DNF or a bad race. I don't think it would have changed much anyway, but at least to finish on the high and having done a good race, scoring nearly 100 points this season. It could have been better, but it's not that bad.”

What the future has in store

Buemi's success behind-the-wheel extends beyond the Formula E paddock, the Swiss driver has won four World Endurance Championship Drivers’ titles, in 2014, 2019, 2022 and 2023, and has claimed four overall victories at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, in 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2022.

With such a prestigious racing CV, there is little doubt that the Swiss driver has a bright future in store - wherever he ends up.

“I guess I'll digest a little bit, the fact that I'm not going to be racing next year," he says. "And then at some point, just really discuss what we can do to get involved with the team and how I can contribute.

“We will do that in the next few weeks and see how we can obviously approach the next season. I'm going to stay in the team as an advisor. I wish I would have been able to continue, but of course there are a lot of things happening with the fact that we have so many races with WEC and it's the way it is.

“I’m wishing the team the very best, I might do a test from time to time, and I'm looking forward to seeing the car on track and hopefully it's going to look good on TV.”

title: Jaguar unveils its first next-gen EV: the Type 01
excerpt:
This week, at its global premiere in New York City, Jaguar gave the world a first look at the beginning of a dramatic new chapter with its all-electric grand tourer, the Type 01.

Now, we've had a complete look at the production model - the iconic British marque's first production car of its rebooted, all-electric era.

It is an ultra-luxury, zero-emission four-door GT with a blistering 0-62mph time of 3.2 seconds, powered by a tri-motor setup that generates an astonishing 1,030PS (1,016bhp) and 1,365Nm of torque.

How fast is the Jaguar Type 01, what's its range and how does it look?

The British manufacturer's new flagship promises up to 400 miles of EPA range (or 450 miles/720km WLTP) courtesy of its 118kWh usable battery pack.

Operating on an ultra-fast 850-volt electrical architecture, it can add 200 miles of range in just 13 minutes when hooked up to a 350kW rapid DC charger.

Built upon the bespoke Jaguar Electric Architecture (JEA), the platform allows for dramatic "exuberant modernist" proportions - featuring a low roofline, elongated bonnet, short front overhang, and massive 23-inch wheels - while maintaining ideal 50:50 weight distribution for sharp dynamic handling.

Drivers benefit from intelligent torque vectoring and active aerodynamics, including active vanes and a three-stage deployable rear spoiler that helps yield a sleek 0.23 drag coefficient.

Jaguar has ensured the Type 01 looks unlike anything else on the road, matching its exterior drama with a rich, tech-forward cabin.

Inside, a central longitudinal spine splits the cabin into four distinct zones, complemented by brass-effect anodised aluminium trim, a single glass 24-inch OLED Interactive Driver Display, a secondary 7-inch touchscreen console, and a full-width Panoramic Soundbar with sensory audio seats.

Type 01: Jaguar's charge into a modern luxury future

Nodding to the brand's heritage while signalling its clean-sheet reset, the "Type" designation honors legendary models like the E-Type, while "0" denotes zero emissions and "1" marks the first vehicle of its new generation.

Leveraging track-to-road engineering insights honed by the double world championship-winning Jaguar TCS Racing Formula E team, Jaguar’s electric power delivery has been calibrated to give deep reserves of rolling power, launching from 62mph to 112mph (100km/h to 180km/h) in just 4.0 seconds.

Designed, engineered, and manufactured in the UK, the Type 01 spearheads Jaguar's transition into a fully electric modern luxury brand. Order books for the four-door grand tourer are set to open in early 2027, with the first client deliveries scheduled for the second half of that year.

What does the Jaguar Type 01 cost and when can you buy one?

Positioning the electric GT firmly in high-end luxury territory, pricing for the Jaguar Type 01 starts from £130,000 ($130,500 in the US), with higher-spec and bespoke builds expected to reach beyond £150,000.

Order books for the British-built flagship are slated to open in early 2027, with first client deliveries scheduled to follow in the second half of the year.

title: COMSOL named Official Multiphysics Partner of Formula E
excerpt:
COMSOL and Formula E have announced a multi-year partnership naming COMSOL the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

The partnership brings together Formula E, the world’s leading all-electric motorsport Championship, and COMSOL, a global leader in multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering (CAE) software. Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics® to investigate complex technology challenges involving multiple interacting physical effects.

Electric race cars bring together electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid, and battery systems under extreme constraints. As Official Multiphysics Partner, COMSOL will support Formula E with simulation software and expertise to help its technology teams understand how interacting physical phenomena influence multiple aspects of the sport. The partnership will also explore how simulation apps and digital twin solutions can make physics-based insight accessible beyond the traditional modeling workflow.

Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said: “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another. We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”

Dan Cherowbrier, CTO at Formula E, said: “Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modeling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing.”

Looking ahead, the next generation of Formula E will place even greater demands on performance, efficiency, energy management, and vehicle development as the Championship prepares for the GEN4 era, introducing the fastest and most technologically advanced race car to date.

At the same time, COMSOL has announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, scheduled for release later this autumn, with new capabilities particularly relevant to advanced engineering workflows, including dedicated electric motor modeling, system-level simulation, agentic modeling, and expanded access for creating simulation apps.

The partnership was announced today at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston, where Cherowbrier delivered a keynote talk on the technology and engineering shaping the future of Formula E. To learn more about the partnership, visit COMSOL's website: www.comsol.com/formula-e.

title: Every race winner of the 2025/26 Formula E Season
excerpt:
São Paulo, Round 1

In the opening round of the 2025/26 Formula E season it was Andretti's Jake Dennis who came out on top after converting pole position into the win in the 2025 Google Cloud São Paulo E-Prix Round 1, though it was anything but a simple lights-to-flag in a hectic 30-lap race.

The Season 9 World Champion had secured Julius Baer Pole Position (following a three-place grid drop for Pascal Wehrlein) and started sharply to lead the pack away. The Brit kept in touch with the leading pack as the race lead changed hands throughout the opening stages, before making it by the Citroen of Nick Cassidy - who'd flown through the pack with a late charge - for what would be the definitive move on Lap 27.

But as the race drew to a close, there was one moment which threatened to overshadow Dennis’ charge to victory, a huge shunt for Formula E rookie Pepe Marti - who flew spectacularly over the top of Jaguar's Antonio Felix da Costa - and thankfully, ultimately, landed safely, meant a late Red Flag and a one-lap sprint to the finish. Dennis was able to hold off reigning champion Oliver Rowland and a charging Nick Cassidy to claim the first win of the season.

Mexico City, Round 2

The 2026 Hankook Mexico City E-Prix will go down in history for French manufacturing giant, Citroën, with the brand securing their first Formula E win, in only their second race in the all-electric championship - and as a nightmare for Season 2 champion, Sebastien Buemi.

REPORT: Nick Cassidy secures Citroën's first Formula E win in Mexico City

Buemi and Envision started the race from pole position, with the DS PENSKE of Taylor Barnard joining him on the front row of the grid. Barnard started well and forced Buemi into defensive manoeuvres in order to keep a hold of P1. The Swiss looked to have done just that but outbraked himself into Turn 1, eventually finding himself all the way down the order in 18th.

Instead it was Nick Cassidy, the master at picking exactly the right moment to pounce and make use of Formula E's two 50kW, all-wheel drive ATTACK MODE power boosts, who was able to take control of the race.

The New Zealander brought his Citroën home first having sliced through the pack for his fourth win in five races. Just behind him, the Mahindra of Edoardo Mortara, who had put the Kiwi under severe pressure by being one of the last drivers to activate his second ATTACK MODE.

Cassidy did hold on though for more silverware after his P3 in the Sao Paulo season-opener, with Mortara's mirrors full of reigning champion Rowland through the sweeping final turn as the top five crossed the line within a second of one-another.

Miami, Round 3

Rain came to the Sunshine State for Round 3, but it didn’t stop Mitch Evans from taking Jaguar TCS Racing’s first win of the 2025/26 season.

The first half of the race proved to be super tricky for the pack, with polesitter Mueller leading away after a Safety Car start - though Andretti's rookie Felipe Drugovich made use of an instant all-wheel drive, 50kW ATTACK MODE activation to climb into P1 in the wet early on.

Mueller found himself back out front after the first round of ATTACK MODE and was able to take advantage of a mishap - as the rain fell harder - between Drugovich and Jaguar TCS Racing's Antonio Felix da Costa behind that took the pair out of race-winning contention.

Amid all that, Evans spied his chance to make progress - clambering through from the back end of the top 10 to the podium positions before a perfect switchback move on Lap 27 saw him by Mueller - the German falling for the dummy move.

From there, the Kiwi was able to manage the lead through the second round of ATTACK MODE activations to a commanding 3.1-second lead come the chequered flag for a record 15th Formula E race win.

Jeddah, Round 4

Formula E returned to Jeddah for Round 4 of the championship and the first double-header of the season. In his 100th E-Prix, Porsche's Pascal Wehrlein sealed a perfectly-executed victory, timing his PIT BOOST and ATTACK MODE just right to head home Mahindra Racing's Edoardo Mortara and Jaguar Racing driver Mitch Evans.

READ: Everything you need to know about PIT BOOST in Formula E

Wehrlein had started the race third and went later than those around him with his 50kW, all-wheel drive ATTACK MODE boost coming after his PIT BOOST stop.The overlap allowed the Season 10 World Champion to pull some eight seconds on those behind heading into the closing stages of the race.

Those who activated ATTACK MODE late seemed the best placed as the race reached its climax. Evans was next to prove as much as he sliced his way through the top 10 to an eventual third at the chequered flag and back-to-back podiums.

Jeddah, Round 5

Antonio Felix da Costa and Jaguar TCS Racing nailed their race strategy to stride to the race win in the 2026 Jeddah E-Prix Round 5, with the Portuguese leading Sebastien Buemi home and reigning champion Oliver Rowland rounding out the podium.

Da Costa was the first of the lead group to leap for both of his mandatory 50kW, all-wheel drive ATTACK MODE boosts and managed to pull a gap on those behind through the second round of activations - enough to hold fast for the win with 2.5 seconds to spare at the chequered flag. Six races in nine for Jaguar and da Costa's first for the team as well as his first since Portland, 2024.

Several drivers cycled the race lead in an energy-critical race, with Buemi one of those - the Swiss eventually winding up second, using an ATTACK MODE overlap to best Rowland who had also led early on.

Madrid, Round 6

Antonio Felix da Costa (Jaguar TCS Racing) became the first and only driver to take more than one victory this season when he stormed to his 14th career win around the Circuito del Jarama.

READ: DAC-TO-DAC: Jaguar's Da Costa debriefs epic Madrid win

Having started third, the 2019/20 Formula E Champion perfectly timed his PIT BOOST and ATTACK MODE activation to rise to the top of the pack. He was on the defensive across the final laps with challenges for the win from his teammate Mitch Evans, CUPRA KIRO’s Dan Ticktum, Porsche’s Pascal Wehrlein and Mahindra Racing’s Edoardo Mortara.

It made for blockbuster viewing, with the grandstands and grassy banks around the circuit packed to the brim with passionate Spanish fans. With Da Costa being Portuguese, and Lisbon a six hour drive from the capital city, he was surrounded by family and friends across the weekend.

Wehrlein leads the Drivers' Championship on 83 points - 11 points clear of Mahindra Racing's Edoardo Mortara. In the Teams' Championship it's tight, with Porsche only 4 points ahead of Jaguar TCS Racing.

Berlin, Round 7

Nico Müller secured a historic maiden victory during the first race of the Berlin E-Prix double-header. On his 69th start in Formula E, the Swiss driver delivered a strategic masterclass to win Porsche's home race in dominant fashion.

Starting from 6th on the grid, Müller focused on energy management during a chaotic opening half, but after his PIT BOOST he made the most of his energy advantage to slice through the grid and build an impressive lead with help from his ATTACK MODE. He finished 4.7 seconds clear of the field to seal a home victory for Porsche and his very first in Formula E, a special moment he shared with his family.

The win was particularly symbolic as Porsche was celebrating the 75th anniversary of Porsche Motorsport. To mark the occasion, Müller’s car ran a special "Pink Pig" livery, a tribute to the legendary Porsche 917/20 from the 1971 24 Hours of Le Mans!

Berlin, Round 8

Jaguar TCS Racing's Mitch Evans timed his push to perfection to take victory at Tempelhof ahead of reigning champion Oliver Rowland and Porsche's Pascal Wehrlein.

The New Zealander started 17th and clambered to the top six by the end of the first round of ATTACK MODE activations with energy in-hand on those around him.

RACE HIGHLIGHTS: 2026 Hankook Berlin E-Prix, Round 8

His initial six-minute 50kW, all-wheel drive ATTACK saw him hit the front on Lap 27 and take control from there, building a gap of two seconds to those behind. He swatted the advances of two World Champions in Rowland and Wehrlein away through the second round of ATTACK MODE as the race reached its climax to seal the deal and his 16th race win in Formula E - more than any other driver in the series' history.

Monaco, Round 9

Mahindra Racing's Nyck de Vries kept his cool around the tight and twisty streets of Monaco to claim his fifth ABB Formula E World Championship race victory, ahead of Jaguar Racing's Mitch Evans and CUPRA KIRO's Pepe Marti.

The Dutch driver started on the front row of the grid, eventually taking the lead of the race with a perfectly executed PIT BOOST strategy, which saw him finish the E-Prix with a comfortable gap to the chasing pack.

De Vries was one of the first drivers to take his PIT BOOST stop, diving into the pits on Lap 16. From there, he smartly timed his ATTACK MODE activation, overtaking then-race leader Antonio Felix da Costa on Lap 20 and remaining unfazed by the fraught battles happening in and around him. From there, he was unchallenged, reaching the chequered flag with a three second gap to the cars behind.

RESULTS: The 2026 Monaco E-Prix Round 9

The victory marks a fifth career win for de Vries, and his first since Berlin 2022 as well as a maiden win with Mahindra - a first for the Indian team in the GEN3 era.

Monaco, Round 10

Nissan's Oliver Rowland assembled the perfect E-Prix to seal victory in Round 10 of the 2025/26 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship in Monaco - navigating the drama to lead home Felipe Drugovich (Andretti) and Antonio Felix da Costa (Jaguar TCS Racing).

Rowland started eighth and came to the fore late on as the ATTACK MODE activations shook out - with the top 10 shuffling and squabbling relentlessly for position throughout the opening half of the race.

The Nissan driver had been strong managing his energy, navigated the pack and picked his way through to the lead down at the Nouvelle Chicane on Lap 23 of 28 - classic Rowland and a second win in two years in Monte Carlo for the Brit.

RESULTS: The 2026 Monaco E-Prix Round 10

A couple of Full Course Yellows were thrown into the mix for Rowland to deal with after some overexhuberant overtaking manoeuvres down the field but the Nissan driver kept cool to cross the line first.

Sanya, Round 11

Jake Dennis and Felipe Drugovich finished as they'd started - with plenty of drama in-between - in the Lianxin Sanya E-Prix Round 11, sealing American team Andretti's first 1-2 in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

The pair steered through a Red Flag and two Full Course Yellows having led away from the front row of the grid to work together and dictate early on. Going later in ATTACK proved to be the way to go as they stamped their authority on the race through the first third and then, most importantly, in the lead up to the chequered flag - having dropped into the pack midway through the encounter.

That was a second win of the season for the Season 9 World Champion, and the second from Julius Baer Pole Position, too. The team followed up a first front-row lockout with that maiden 1-2. CUPRA KIRO's Pepe Marti produced a wonder-drive from all but last at the Red Flag restart to third in effectively just 17 racing laps - the Spaniard also following up maiden silverware in Monte Carlo with another trophy here.

UPDATE: Drugovich hit with five-second time penalty, loses podium finish

However, there was more drama to come after the flag. Drugovich was hit with a five-second time penalty for contact with Wehrlein that was judged to have been avoidable by race stewards. This meant that Marti was promoted to a career-best second place, while Nyck de Vries inherited third position.

Shanghai, Round 12

Porsche's Pascal Wehrlein strode to victory in the Shanghai E-Prix Round 12, timing PIT BOOST to perfection, just before the weather closed in - ending the German's three-race pointless streak.

The polesitter won the battle for track position, as drivers and engineers pushed for the front with rain on the horizon. Heading through the PIT BOOST window, he emerged out front before a Safety Car was required as the rain fell hard on Lap 19.

The Season 10 World Champion was able to stride clear of the pack from there to the chequered flag with Antonio Felix da Costa (Jaguar TCS Racing) and Jake Dennis (Andretti) unable to prevent Wehrlein sealing a 10th career victory.

RESULTS: The 2026 Shanghai E-Prix Round 12

Felipe Drugovich followed Dennis home as the Andrettis played the team game to secure P3 and P4 through the final few laps. Nyck de Vries followed for Mahindra, climbing all the way from P16 to fifth at the flag. Jean-Eric Vergne came sixth after a tidy E-Prix for Citroen Racing.

Shanghai, Round 13

Drying conditions favoured the brave as those that gambled with the setup on their cars were able to slice through the field to the podium, and none profited more than ultra-experienced Brazilian Lucas di Grassi who had started the race in 18th position.

Joel Eriksson (Envision Racing) had led the pack away from a late caution with Jean-Eric Vergne (Citroen Racing) and di Grassi in close company - the trio all up 16 spots from the start at this stage. Crucially, that Full Course Yellow had neutralised Eriksson and Vergne's ATTACK MODE activations, with di Grassi's still in-hand.

RESULTS: The 2026 Shanghai E-Prix Round 13

The 2016/17 champion duly used his remaining 50kW, all-wheel drive boost once the FCY ended to make up ground on the pair ahead, passing Eriksson at the hairpin on the penultimate lap as Vergne fought through to the lead - before dispatching the Citroen driver half a lap later at Turn 1, on the final lap, for the win.

That was a first trip to the top step of the podium since 2022 for di Grassi, who also won the very first Formula E race, also here in China back in 2014. He remains Formula E's oldest race winner at now 41 years 328 days old and he sets a new record as the series' oldest podium finisher. Vergne came home second in the end with Eriksson following for his best finish yet, and a maiden podium.

Tokyo, Round 14

CUPRA KIRO's Dan Ticktum pounced through the penultimate corner to steal victory from Jake Dennis in the first Tokyo night race; with the pair heading home Nick Cassidy who sealed an emotional podium for Citroen Racing in the 2026 TDK Tokyo E-Prix Round 14.

Ticktum started sixth and went early with both PIT BOOST and ATTACK MODE to emerge from the stops as the net leader. Dennis, though, had the overlap on the rest with his 50kW, all-wheel drive boost and by the end of Lap 29, he made it by Cassidy then Ticktum to hit the front. From there, it looked to be comfortable, with Ticktum also seeming to settle for a strong second with a message over Team Radio.

RESULTS: The 2026 TDK Tokyo E-Prix Round 14

However, right at the last - through the penultimate turn, ahead of the final chicane, Ticktum spied his chance to jump Dennis as the Andretti driver lifted early with energy critical. He made the move stick and led his compatriot home to make it nine different winners in the last nine rounds, with the closest winning margin of the season - his second in Formula E.

Tokyo, Round 15

Mahindra Racing's Nyck de Vries got his setup just right to fire from fifth to victory in the 2026 TDK Tokyo E-Prix Round 15 in mixed conditions, heading home Citroen Racing's Nick Cassidy and Andretti's Jake Dennis, with title contenders Pascal Wehrlein and Mitch Evans failing to score.

De Vries made a timely jump for ATTACK on Lap 28 and picked off those ahead to reach reigning champion Oliver Rowland in P1; the Nissan driver himself on a late charge. The Brit elected not to match de Vries up with his own final of two mandatory 50kW all-wheel drive ATTACK MODE activations, and that proved costly as de Vries made it by Rowland through the middle sector of that same tour.

RESULTS: The 2026 TDK Tokyo E-Prix Round 15

Mahindra had opted to set the car up for a drying surface, gambling on further rain holding off after a deluge earlier in the afternoon. De Vries navigated a late Red Flag for a second win of 2025/26 and Mahindra's second of the season; a feat the team hadn't achieved since 2017/18.

Dennis, staggeringly, clambered from 17th to the final spot on the podium thanks to a late ATTACK MODE charge. That sees him top of the Drivers' World Championship heading to the site of his first title victory in London and the finale weekend.

The Season 9 champion was able to take advantage of Pascal Werhlein's misery, with a second non-score for the Porsche driver in as many rounds in Tokyo leaving him third in the running. Mitch Evans (Jaguar TCS Racing) failed to finish today, too, and having provisionally led the running earlier in the race, he leaves Tokyo two points behind Dennis in second.

London, Round 16

Polesitter Wehrlein's ultimately dominant third win of the season was sealed during the PIT BOOST window. Werhlein was able to make use of a timely Full Course Yellow (FCY) - thrown for the recovery of Lucas di Grassi's Lola Yamaha ABT - to make what effectively became a free pit stop with the pack neutralised by the caution.

RESULTS: The 2026 Hankook London E-Prix Round 16

Mitch Evans had been looking to mount a challenge from third despite the Porsches of Wehrlein and Mueller working together, against him, early on. Jaguar TCS Racing switched up his strategy to clear Mueller with an early ATTACK MODE deployment and PIT BOOST stop - forcing leader Werhlein to counter. The FCY put paid to Evans' charge, though, and left the Kiwi marooned 21 points back in the standings in third spot.

Dennis was another of several drivers that pitted during FCY and elected to take his ATTACK late to clamber from the cusp of the top six to second at the flag with moves by da Costa and Ticktum key in limiting Wehrlein's new gap at the top of the Drivers' standings to five points.

London, Round 17

The destination of the crown changed hands three times in as many corners, as Andretti's Jake Dennis made a late charge from the back of the pack with Wehrlein coming under severe pressure from Antonio Felix da Costa (Jaguar TCS Racing), who did his bit in his teammate's fight for the title, and in Jaguar's battle for Teams' honours.

At the end of Lap 27, Wehrlein was told by his race engineer to let a charging Sebastien Buemi (Envision Racing) past but that, and a squeeze from da Costa, left the pre-race standings leader shuffled all the way to 12th and outside the points with Dennis able to make it by for eighth, enough to the top of the points table, through his first ATTACK MODE while Evans sat fourth.

Ultimately, Evans could climb no higher, having bided his time to take ATTACK MODE; the Mahindras and Barnard had gapped the Jaguar driver and the rest out-front. A win was the only outcome that would have seen the Kiwi take the crown, even with Wehrlein being once again shuffled down the order and out of the points-paying positions by his own contact with Envision Racing's Joel Eriksson at Turn 16 on Lap 31.

The ensuing chaos handed caught out Dennis too, and the Brit was eliminated from the race and title contention with damage to his car caused in the melee.

Barnard's late ATTACK MODE activation saw him able to muscle by Mortara for P2, then polesitter de Vries for the win with a sneaky dive up the inside of the Season 8 champion into the final turn with just two laps left to run. The Brit was able to convert to become the youngest Formula E race winner at 22 years and 76 days old, superseding Maximilian Guenther, on DS Automobiles final Formula E outing.

title: Every Formula E Driver Who Has Won Their Home E-Prix
excerpt:
Feature by Katy Fairman

Across 12 seasons of Formula E, only a select few can say they’ve been victorious on home soil. Winning your home event is a special – and rare – achievement, and often a dream for most drivers, but how often has that happened in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship?

From nerve-wracking overtakes on iconic city streets to emotional maiden victories, a select group of drivers have overcome the immense pressure of their home crowds to take the chequered flag. Here are the elite Formula E drivers who delivered unforgettable victories on home turf.

Jake Dennis in London (2021 and 2022)

Standing on the top step at your home race is a rare feat, but Andretti’s Jake Dennis has managed it twice and is the only person on this list to do so.

During the London E-Prix in both the 2020/21 and 2021/22 seasons, Dennis dominated the opening race of both double-headers. In 2021, he converted a front-row start into a decisive victory, finishing over five seconds clear of Nyck de Vries. The following year, Dennis delivered a commanding lights-to-flag win over Stoffel Vandoorne, then backed it up with a second-place finish the next day on London's unique indoor-outdoor circuit.

While he missed out on a hat-trick of London wins in 2022/23, Dennis clinched the Drivers’ World Championship at the ExCeL London instead—becoming the first British driver in Formula E history to secure the crown on home soil.

Jean-Eric Vergne in Paris (2018)

Citroën Racing’s Jean-Éric Vergne claimed a memorable home victory during the 2018 Paris E-Prix. Starting from pole position, the Frenchman kept his composure on the streets of Paris, fending off Sam Bird and André Lotterer through mid-race car swaps to secure the win with the Eiffel Tower in the background.

Calling it the "most emotional" victory of his career, Vergne admitted he couldn't even speak as he crossed the finish line. The win was a special birthday milestone in a dominant year that saw him go on to claim his first Drivers' Championship.

Vergne repeated his title glory in the following season, making him the only back-to-back champion in Formula E history. Très bien, JEV!

Taylor Barnard in London (2026)

The most recent addition to this list is Taylor Barnard, who became Formula E’s youngest-ever winner when he took his maiden victory at the final race of the 2025/26 in London.

Surrounded by friends and family, the young Briton was able to pass both Mahindra’s as the race drew to a close and added his name into the record books as the World Championship’s youngest winner aged 22 years, two months and 15 days. Racing for DS PENSKE, Barnard’s silverware also meant that all teams recorded at least one podium result and all but one team achieved a victory across the season.

Maximilian Guenther in Berlin (2020)

During the 2019/20 campaign, Maximilian Guenther claimed a thrilling victory on home soil at the Berlin E-Prix while driving for BMW i Andretti Motorsport.

Competing at the Tempelhof Airport circuit, Guenther executed a daring pass on Jean-Éric Vergne for the lead with just four minutes remaining. Ignoring team instructions to wait until the final lap, the German made the move stick to secure his second career Formula E win.

The tense victory showcased his huge potential, and Guenther has since added five more wins – seven total – to his resume, most recently taking top honors at the 2025 Shanghai E-Prix for DS PENSKE but moves to Paysafe Envision Racing for GEN4.

Sam Bird in London (2015)

Having been a part of Formula E since its inaugural season, Sam Bird has had plenty of opportunities to lock in a home win. Nevertheless, he didn't need it, as he won the London E-Prix in Formula E's very first season.

Navigating himself around the picturesque Battersea Park in England's capital, Bird won the final round of Season 1 in 2015. Repping Virgin Racing at the time, the Briton - born not at all far away in Roehampton - ended his maiden season on a high.

“What a way to finish [the season],” Bird said at the time. “Unbelievable, unbelievable. The race today was a great race, starting from fourth. We were very strong and I was able to attack people into Turn 11, and we made the moves stick which is nice.”

Oliver Rowland in London (2024)

Prior to his London win in 2024, Oliver Rowland had never scored a single point at a home E-Prix.

After missing the penultimate round in Portland due to illness, Rowland was out of championship contention, allowing him to race without pressure. He stayed patient in the lead group, capitalising as the title contenders battled around him to swoop ahead and cross the line first.

The breakthrough home win proved to be a sign of things to come, setting the stage for Rowland to go on and claim the 2024/25 Drivers' World Championship.

Daniel Abt in Berlin (2018)

Audi Sport ABT Schaeffler's Daniel Abt was on a mission during 2018’s race around Berlin’s historic Tempelhof Airport Circuit. Having achieved his maiden victory four races before in Mexico City, Abt was ready to repeat his success at his and Audi's home race.

Abt signed off a career-defining race weekend with a commanding lights-to-flag win on home soil at the popular venue. He also claimed pole position and the fastest lap – a then-unique feat in Formula E.

As well as Abt’s first place, his teammate Lucas di Grassi, was able to finish in second making it an Audi 1-2 result at their home event.

Alex Lynn in London (2021)

Representing Mahindra Racing, Alex Lynn secured a memorable home victory during the 2021 London E-Prix double-header, following Jake Dennis' win the previous day.

After finishing third on Saturday, Lynn took the top step just 24 hours later, earning his first and only victory in Formula E. Four years after earning pole position on his debut in New York City, the Briton finally tasted champagne on home soil at the Excel Arena.

The emotional breakthrough sparked wild celebrations in the pit lane, with Team Principal Dilbagh Gill famously leaping for joy as Lynn crossed the chequered flag to complete back-to-back British wins.

The 2026/27 Formula E season will commence in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on December 18 & 19.

title: Andretti Formula E names Campbell Hobson as new Team Principal
excerpt:
Campbell Hobson will replace longtime team leader Roger Griffiths, who transitions into a senior advisory role at Andretti.

Campbell Hobson will replace longtime team leader Roger Griffiths, who transitions into a senior advisory role at Andretti.

Australian-born Hobson is no stranger to the Andretti squad, having played an integral role in the day-to-day running of the team as their Team Manager, and later Sporting Director. His appointment comes at an exciting time for Andretti Formula E, as the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship prepares to enter the GEN4 era - the fastest and most exciting chapter to-date.

“Campbell has been instrumental in the operation, and we are very happy to see him take this opportunity to lead the team,” said Jill Gregory, President of Andretti Global and Chief Operating Officer of TWG Motorsports. “He knows the program inside and out, has the respect of the team and brings the leadership and competitive drive we need as we look toward the future.”

Hobson replaces Roger Griffiths, one of the paddock's most respected figures, who leaves the role to step into a new senior advisory position supporting Andretti Formula E and the broader TWG Motorsports portfolio. He leaves behind quite the legacy, with 13 victories, 46 podiums and a Drivers’ World Championship with Jake Dennis all happening under his leadership.

“Leading this team from the beginning has been one of the great privileges of my career, and I’m incredibly proud of what we’ve built,” said Griffiths. “After 12 seasons, this feels like the right time to pass the torch. Campbell has been a trusted part of our leadership for years and understands this organization at every level; he has earned this opportunity. I’m excited to support him while also contributing more broadly across Andretti and TWG Motorsports.”
